topics.title: Supreme Court ruling on the definition of industry draws Congress concern
why_in_news: **Congress** criticised the **Supreme Court** majority judgment in **State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh**, delivered on **August 20, 2026**, for potentially narrowing the legal meaning of “industry”. The controversy concerns the court’s reconsideration of the broad approach adopted in **Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa** (**1978**), which formulated the Triple Test.

header: Key legal position mentioned in the report
rows: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa
Industry involves systematic activity, employer–employee cooperation, and production or distribution of goods or services; absence of profit motive is not by itself decisive.
State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh
The majority introduced a requirement of discernible commercial character and widened the possible sovereign-function exclusion.

key_details.text: The majority clarified that its reformulation would not disturb concluded or pending proceedings under the erstwhile **Industrial Disputes Act**, and would not govern interpretation of the **Industrial Relations Code, 2020**. **Jairam Ramesh** argued that leaving the issue open could create uncertainty before Labour Courts and Industrial Tribunals. Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** dissented, supporting the settled **1978** position.

static_linkage.summary: This updates the static topics of the definition of “industry”, judicial interpretation of labour legislation, industrial relations and the role of the Supreme Court in settling precedent.

blocks.title: What it is
items: “Industry” identifies organised activities to which statutory industrial-dispute protections apply. The term was defined in **Section 2(j), Industrial Disputes Act 1947**, and is separately defined in **Section 2(p), Industrial Relations Code 2020**. The **Supreme Court** settles the authoritative interpretation of the statutory definition through binding precedent.

blocks.title: Key facts
rows: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa (1978)
State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh (2026)
Dissenting judge in Jai Bir Singh

blocks.title: The provisions that get asked
items: **Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa (1978)** formulated the **Triple Test**: systematic activity, cooperation between employer and employee, and production or distribution of goods or services to satisfy human wants and wishes.
Absence of a profit motive does not, by itself, exclude an activity from the definition of **industry**.

Core sovereign functions, including **judiciary**, **law and order** and **defence**, fall outside the ordinary concept of industry; the nature of the function, rather than the label of the organisation, is decisive.
**State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh (2026)** introduced a requirement of discernible commercial character and widened the possible exclusion of sovereign functions.

The majority in **Jai Bir Singh (2026)** stated that its reformulation would not disturb concluded or pending proceedings under the erstwhile **Industrial Disputes Act 1947**, and would not govern interpretation of the **Industrial Relations Code 2020**.

items: **Industrial Disputes Act 1947** vs **Industrial Relations Code 2020** — the former is the earlier framework whose definition appears in **Section 2(j)**; the latter is the successor framework with its own definition in **Section 2(p)**.

**Bangalore Water Supply (1978)** vs **Jai Bir Singh (2026)** — the former applies the broad **Triple Test**; the latter adds discernible commercial character and a wider sovereign-function exclusion.
**Labour Courts** vs **Industrial Tribunals** — both adjudicate industrial disputes, but they are distinct statutory adjudicatory forums under labour legislation.

topics.title: Supreme Court sets aside NGT order holding Art of Living Foundation responsible for Yamuna floodplain damage
tags: GROUP-II PAPER II — SCIENCE, ENVIRONMENT & HEALTH
why_in_news: **Supreme Court** set aside the **December 2017** order of the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** that held **Sri Sri Ravi Shankar’s Art of Living Foundation** responsible for damage to the **Yamuna floodplains** during its **World Culture Festival**, held in **2016**. The appeal was filed by **Vyakti Vikas Kendra India**, associated with the foundation.

rows: Delhi Development Authority (DDA) was criticised for permitting the event on an active floodplain.
The permission was held inconsistent with the precautionary principle and the doctrine of public trust.
DDA was directed to refund Rs. 5 crore deposited by the foundation within four weeks.
DDA must continue rehabilitation of the Yamuna floodplains in accordance with the plan and directions of the NGT.

key_details.text: The Court noted that the floodplain had already been damaged before it was handed over to the foundation and that the **NGT** had not considered relevant material, including the foundation’s letter referring to debris and construction material at the site. The judgment therefore separates responsibility for prior damage from the continuing duty of public authorities to restore the ecosystem.

static_linkage.summary: This updates the static topics of environmental governance, green jurisprudence, judicial review and the functioning of specialised tribunals. It illustrates how constitutional environmental principles guide administrative permissions and restoration duties.

blocks.title: What it is
items: Environmental governance in India combines constitutional duties, statutory regulation and judicial remedies. The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)**, established under the **National Green Tribunal Act 2010**, is a specialised tribunal for environmental disputes, compensation and restoration; the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** exercise constitutional review over environmental decision-making. The **Delhi Development Authority (DDA)** is a statutory authority constituted under the **Delhi Development Act 1957**, responsible for planned development in Delhi, including regulation of land-use permissions.

blocks.title: Key facts
rows: Article 21 — right to life, including environmental quality
Article 48A — State duty to protect and improve the environment
Article 51A(g) — citizen’s duty to protect the natural environment

blocks.title: The provisions that get asked
items: **Section 14, National Green Tribunal Act 2010** gives the NGT jurisdiction over civil cases involving a substantial question relating to the environment, including enforcement of a legal right relating to the environment.
**Section 15** empowers the NGT to provide relief and compensation to victims of pollution, restitution of damaged property and restitution of the environment.
**Section 16** gives the NGT appellate jurisdiction over specified orders and decisions made under the enactments listed in Schedule I to the Act.
**Section 20** requires the NGT to apply the principles of sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
**Section 22** provides an appeal from an NGT order to the **Supreme Court** only on a question of law, ordinarily within **90 days**.

The public trust doctrine treats rivers, forests, wetlands and other natural resources as resources held by the State in trust for the public and future generations; the precautionary principle permits preventive action despite incomplete scientific certainty.

topics.title: Researchers report a 3.5-billion-year-old microbial biosignature in Indian rock
why_in_news: **Researchers** have reported evidence that microbial life existed at least **3.5 billion years ago** in what is now eastern India. The evidence comes from a carbon-bearing, black-and-white banded chert from **Bhitardari** in the **Singhbhum Craton**, an ancient continental block extending across parts of **Jharkhand** and **Odisha**.

key_details.text: The study appeared in the peer-reviewed **Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences**. Researchers used uranium-lead dating of zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Four of the eight zircons analysed indicated an age of **3,497 million years**; the crystals were interpreted as volcanic ash deposited while the chert formed. The biological interpretation rests on several converging clues: the carbon isotope pattern resembles carbon captured by living cells, and the carbon appeared to be degraded organic matter rather than later inorganic contamination. Chert, a silica-rich fine-grained rock, can preserve organic material for very long periods but cannot itself be dated directly. The work is significant because the **Earth** formed about **4.54 billion years ago**, suggesting that life may have emerged relatively early in planetary history. Older proposed evidence from **Greenland** rocks, dated to **3.7–3.8 billion years**, remains disputed.

static_linkage.summary: This item updates the static topics of Precambrian geology, cratons, rock formation and radiometric dating, while also connecting earth science with theories on the origin and early evolution of life.

blocks.title: What it is
items: The **Veligonda Project**, also called the **Poola Subbaiah Veligonda Project**, is an irrigation and drinking-water project of the **Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Department**. It conveys **Krishna**-basin water from the **Srisailam Reservoir** through tunnels across the **Nallamala** region to drought-prone areas of **Andhra Pradesh**, particularly **Prakasam**, **Nellore**, **Kadapa** and **Markapuram** districts.

blocks.title: The provisions that get asked
items: Irrigation, canals, drainage and embankments within a State fall mainly under **State List, Entry 17**, subject to **Union List, Entry 56**, which permits Union regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys in the public interest.

**Article 262** empowers **Parliament** to provide for adjudication of disputes relating to the waters of inter-State rivers and river valleys and to exclude the jurisdiction of courts over such disputes.
The **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** provides the statutory framework for adjudicating qualifying inter-State river-water disputes through tribunals.

**Polavaram Project** is a multipurpose project on the **Godavari**; its canal system is associated with transfer of Godavari water towards the **Krishna** system, whereas **Veligonda** conveys **Krishna**-basin water from **Srisailam**.

Under the **Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013**, compensation and rehabilitation-and-resettlement entitlements are distinct protections for project-affected families and project oustees.

blocks.title: Easily confused with
items: **Veligonda Project** — a **Krishna**-basin tunnel project linked to **Srisailam**; **Polavaram Project** — a **Godavari** project associated with inter-basin transfer towards the **Krishna** system.
**Srisailam** — a reservoir and multipurpose project on the **Krishna**; **Nagarjuna Sagar** — a separate dam and irrigation project downstream on the same river.

blocks.title: Andhra Pradesh
items: **Rayalaseema** is a drought-prone region of **Andhra Pradesh**; projects such as **Veligonda** and **Polavaram-linked water transfer** are associated with regional irrigation and agricultural development.
**Ramayapatnam Port** provides a coastal export linkage for horticultural and agricultural produce from the project-command and adjoining regions.
